request.summary: Prove that editable Wayfinding Studio projects can publish portable v1 and v2 map packages that power a multi-building, multi-level Wallboard wayfinding app in 2D, 3D, atlas, and exploded overview modes.
request.audience: Visitors using a landscape touch display at a modern campus.
request.primaryGoal: Let a visitor search globally, inspect or enter buildings, and follow one continuous outdoor-to-indoor journey across entrances and vertical connectors without losing context.

assumptions: The Northline campus data is synthetic and license-safe.
Each checked-in .wbwayfinding project is an editable source and each bundled .wbmap is its published runtime package.
The v1 reference proves backward-compatible loading; the v2 venue proves the Site to Buildings to Levels contract.
The primary surfaces are Full HD and 1366x768 landscape touch displays.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The map and touch directory form a deliberate landscape kiosk composition.

ownership.rationale: Reviewed geometry, hierarchy, connectors, graph topology, destination content, and media are authored and published together as portable runtime packages.
Operators control kiosk identity and safe presentation choices without changing reviewed geometry.
Venue focus, journey progression, and camera movement belong to the active visitor session.

views.purpose: Rotate, pan, zoom, select extruded spaces, and inspect the route.
Use the same artifact as a legible architectural map with directional route flow and turn-by-turn guidance.
Show only the site and route-relevant building levels together for complete journey comprehension.
Keep unrelated buildings collapsed while expanding the route-relevant aligned floors above their footprint.

inputs.action: Rotate, pan, zoom, and select destinations.
Search globally, focus a building, explore inside, request directions, advance a journey, or reset.

session.expectation: Reset clears destination selection and restores the authored 3D camera.

rendering.rationale: The map owns all available space beside a fixed, readable directory.

motion.rationale: The current position pulses while visitor camera movement remains direct and touch-controlled.

branding.provenance: Northline is a fictional campus identity controlled through safe operator settings.

settings.purpose: Allows visitors to switch between the two renderers.
Controls current-position pulse without changing direct visitor camera control.
Selects the coordinated Light, Dark, or Custom palette.

dynamicText.fallback: Keep the complete name where space permits and use one-line ellipsis only after the readable floor.
dynamicText.rationale: The kiosk identity must stay readable without changing header height.

dynamicText.fallback: Wrap names to two lines and scroll the directory instead of shrinking below the touch-readable floor.

states.expectation: The nonblank 3D map, complete directory, and authored camera fill the Full-HD kiosk.
The same interaction remains readable at 1366x768.
The 2D renderer keeps all authored spaces legible, emphasizes the selected destination, and presents the shared route with direction and journey steps.
The coordinated dark interface keeps the 3D scene and directory legible.
The v2 site shows three selectable buildings, globally searchable interior destinations, and a touch-friendly building card.
Building directions show the site plus only that building's relevant levels and one continuous route.
The selected three-floor building expands above its aligned footprint while other buildings remain collapsed.

behaviors.expectation: The packaged custom app renders nonblank WebGL from the Studio artifact.
Destination selection drives the same graph route in 3D and 2D, with a floor-independent origin and floor-aware journey guidance.
Global building and destination selection drives continuous outdoor, entrance, indoor, and vertical route legs through atlas and exploded views.
Calibrated route geometry produces deterministic turn, transition, and arrival steps without showing false zero-distance guidance.
Reset clears selection and restores the authored camera without recreating the app.

visualDirection.summary: A warm architectural venue rather than a dashboard: site context, legible aligned interiors, route-relevant atlas cards, exploded floor stacks, and one compact global directory.
signatureChoices: The semantic floor model is the full-bleed primary object rather than a card.
Each destination has a distinct architectural color and Studio-authored height.
avoid: Decorative perspective that blocks route inspection

visualReview.intent: A convincing real custom-app proof that an editable Studio project can publish a touch-controlled spatial wayfinding product.
focus: Verify the WebGL canvas is nonblank and correctly framed.
Verify labels float above their matching extrusions without clipping.
Verify route and selection remain obvious in both 2D and 3D.
Verify the site, building card, atlas, journey controls, and exploded floor stack preserve context across scene changes.
Verify no control or directory text overlaps at either accepted surface.
